claim: Advances in single-cell sequencing technologies have provided novel insights into the dynamics of gene expression and cellular heterogeneity within tissues.
source: Advances in single-cell sequencing technologies have provided novel insights into the dynamics of gene expression and cellular heterogeneity within tissues and have enabled the construction of transcriptomic cell atlases.
evidence: This is a general statement about the capabilities of single-cell sequencing technologies, representing established knowledge in the field.

claim: Single-cell sequencing technologies have enabled the construction of transcriptomic cell atlases.
source: Advances in single-cell sequencing technologies have provided novel insights into the dynamics of gene expression and cellular heterogeneity within tissues and have enabled the construction of transcriptomic cell atlases.
evidence: This statement reflects established knowledge about the application of single-cell sequencing in creating cell atlases.

claim: Linking anatomical information to transcriptomic data and positively identifying the cell types that correspond to gene expression clusters in single-cell sequencing data sets remains a challenge.
source: However, linking anatomical information to transcriptomic data and positively identifying the cell types that correspond to gene expression clusters in single-cell sequencing data sets remains a challenge.
evidence: This is a statement about current limitations in the field, representing established knowledge about challenges in single-cell sequencing analysis.

claim: TaG-EM involves inserting a DNA barcode just upstream of the polyadenylation site in a Gal4-inducible UAS-GFP construct.
source: This method, called Targeted Genetically-Encoded Multiplexing (TaG-EM), involves inserting a DNA barcode just upstream of the polyadenylation site in a Gal4-inducible UAS-GFP construct so that the barcode sequence can be read out during single-cell sequencing, labeling a cell population of interest.
evidence: This describes the technical design of the TaG-EM method developed in this study.

claim: TaG-EM barcode sequences can be read out during single-cell sequencing.
source: This method, called Targeted Genetically-Encoded Multiplexing (TaG-EM), involves inserting a DNA barcode just upstream of the polyadenylation site in a Gal4-inducible UAS-GFP construct so that the barcode sequence can be read out during single-cell sequencing, labeling a cell population of interest.
evidence: This is a claim about the functionality of TaG-EM that is demonstrated in the manuscript's experiments.

claim: TaG-EM enables positive identification of cell types in cell atlas projects.
source: By creating many such independently barcoded fly strains, TaG-EM enables positive identification of cell types in cell atlas projects, identification of multiplet droplets, and barcoding of experimental timepoints, conditions, and replicates.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing TaG-EM barcodes labeling specific cell populations in single-cell sequencing experiments.

claim: TaG-EM enables identification of multiplet droplets.
source: By creating many such independently barcoded fly strains, TaG-EM enables positive identification of cell types in cell atlas projects, identification of multiplet droplets, and barcoding of experimental timepoints, conditions, and replicates.
evidence: This is supported by data showing TaG-EM identified 100 additional doublets beyond computational methods.

claim: TaG-EM barcodes can be read out using next-generation sequencing to facilitate population-scale behavioral measurements.
source: Furthermore, we demonstrate that TaG-EM barcodes can be read out using next-generation sequencing to facilitate population-scale behavioral measurements.
evidence: This is demonstrated through phototaxis, oviposition, and gut motility experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: Spatially and temporally regulated gene expression patterns are a hallmark of multicellular life.
source: Spatially and temporally regulated gene expression patterns are a hallmark of multicellular life and function to orchestrate patterning, growth, and differentiation throughout development (Ingham, 1988; Reeves et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a general statement about developmental biology supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Spatial expression patterns define functionally distinct compartments in mature organisms.
source: In mature organisms, spatial expression patterns both in tissues and within cells define functionally distinct compartments and determine many aspects of cellular and organismal physiology (Martin and Ephrussi, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Expression patterns differentiate healthy and diseased tissue and impact disease etiology.
source: In addition, such expression patterns differentiate healthy and diseased tissue and impact disease etiology (Marusyk et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Single-cell sequencing technologies have provided insights into the dynamics of gene expression throughout development.
source: Single-cell sequencing technologies have provided insights into the dynamics of gene expression throughout development, been used to characterize somatic variation and heterogeneity within tissues, and are currently enabling the construction of transcriptomic cell atlases (Klein et al., 2015; Macosko et al., 2015; Zheng et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The cellular identities of gene expression clusters identified in cell atlas data sets are typically inferred from the expression of distinctive gene sets.
source: The cellular identities of gene expression clusters identified in cell atlas data sets are typically inferred from the expression of distinctive gene sets (Hung et al., 2020; Li et al., 2022; Ma et al., 2021), and the lack of positive identification of gene expression clusters introduces an element of uncertainty in this analysis.
evidence: This describes current practice in the field, supported by citations.

claim: The lack of positive identification of gene expression clusters introduces an element of uncertainty in cell atlas analysis.
source: The cellular identities of gene expression clusters identified in cell atlas data sets are typically inferred from the expression of distinctive gene sets (Hung et al., 2020; Li et al., 2022; Ma et al., 2021), and the lack of positive identification of gene expression clusters introduces an element of uncertainty in this analysis.
evidence: This is an inference about limitations of current methods based on established knowledge.

claim: Manual annotation of cell clusters is labor-intensive and often requires additional experiments to determine or confirm the expression patterns of marker genes.
source: Moreover, this process of manual annotation is labor-intensive and often requires additional experiments to determine or confirm the expression patterns of marker genes.
evidence: This describes a practical limitation of current methods based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: Antibody-based cell hashing approaches have been developed to allow multiplexing of samples in droplet-based single-cell sequencing reactions.
source: Antibody-based cell hashing or feature barcoding approaches have been developed to allow multiplexing of samples in droplet-based single-cell sequencing reactions (Stoeckius et al., 2018; Stoeckius et al., 2017).
evidence: This describes existing methods in the field, supported by citations.

claim: Antibody-based multiplexing strategies typically barcode samples at a population level and do not enable labeling of cell subpopulations within a sample.
source: While such approaches can reduce per-sample costs, typically samples are barcoded at a population level and thus do not enable labeling of cell subpopulations within a sample.
evidence: This describes a limitation of existing methods based on established knowledge.

claim: A pool containing 29 unique barcode-containing plasmids was injected into Drosophila embryos for PhiC31-mediated integration.
source: A pool containing 29 unique barcode-containing plasmids was injected into Drosophila embryos for PhiC31-mediated integration into the attP2 landing site (Groth et al., 2004) and transgenic lines were isolated and confirmed by Sanger sequencing (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the experimental procedure used to generate TaG-EM lines.

claim: 20 distinctly barcoded Drosophila lines were recovered from the pool injection.
source: We recovered 20 distinctly barcoded Drosophila lines, with some barcodes recovered from multiple crosses (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental results.

claim: TaG-EM measurements are highly accurate and reproducible.
source: The resulting data indicated that TaG-EM measurements are highly accurate and reproducible.
evidence: This conclusion is based on structured pool experiments showing consistent results across technical replicates.

claim: Technical replicates of TaG-EM measurements showed minimal variability.
source: Technical replicates (indicated by error bars in Figure 2B–E) showed minimal variability.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Three independently extracted replicates of the even pools produced consistent data with all 20 barcodes detected at levels close to the expected 5% abundance.
source: Likewise, the three independently extracted replicates of the even pools produced consistent data with all 20 barcodes detected at levels close to the expected 5% abundance (Figure 2B–C).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B-C.

claim: For staggered pools, R2 values were >0.99 when multiple barcodes for an input level were averaged.
source: For the staggered pools, abundances correlated well with the expected values, particularly when multiple barcodes for an input level were averaged, in which case R2 values were >0.99 (Figure 2D–E, inset plots).
evidence: This is directly supported by data shown in Figure 2D-E.

claim: A high level of quantitative accuracy can be attained using sequencing-based analysis of TaG-EM barcode abundance, particularly when averaging data for three to four independent barcodes for an experimental condition.
source: This indicates that a high level of quantitative accuracy can be attained using sequencing-based analysis of TaG-EM barcode abundance, particularly when averaging data for three to four independent barcodes for an experimental condition.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the structured pool experiments showing high R2 values.

claim: Preference indices calculated for pooled, NGS-based TaG-EM measurements were nearly identical to conventional behavioral measurements for both wild type and norpA mutants in phototaxis assays.
source: Preference indices calculated for the pooled, NGS-based TaG-EM measurements were nearly identical to conventional behavioral measurements for both wild type and norpA mutants (Figure 3A–B).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data comparing TaG-EM and video-based measurements shown in Figure 3A-B.

claim: TaG-EM barcode 14 had reduced barcode abundance across multiple oviposition trials.
source: In general, TaG-EM measurements of oviposition correlated with fly numbers, with the exception of barcode 14 which had reduced barcode abundance across multiple trials (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an observation from experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Despite TaG-EM barcode constructs being inserted in a common landing site, differences with respect to specific behaviors may exist among the lines.
source: This suggests that despite the fact that the genetic barcode constructs are inserted in a common landing site, differences with respect to specific behaviors may exist among the lines, and thus one should test to make sure given lines are appropriate to use in specific behavioral assays.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of barcode 14's poor performance.

claim: Manually scored viable egg numbers and TaG-EM barcode abundances were well correlated across two independent experimental trials (R2 values of 0.52–0.61 for Trial 1 and 0.74–0.84 for Trial 2).
source: Manually scored viable egg numbers and TaG-EM barcode abundances were well correlated across two independent experimental trials (R2 values of 0.52–0.61 for Trial 1 and 0.74–0.84 for Trial 2).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: When barcodes from each individual timepoint were averaged, R2 values for the correlation between manual and sequencing-based measurements were 0.95 for Trial 1 and 0.99 for Trial 2 in age-dependent fecundity experiments.
source: When barcodes from each individual timepoint were averaged, R2 values for the correlation between manual and sequencing-based measurements were 0.95 for Trial 1 and 0.99 for Trial 2 (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Caffeine reduces transit time through the larval gut.
source: Using the manual assay, we observed that while caffeine-containing food is aversive to larvae, the presence of caffeine reduces transit time through the gut (Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The effect of caffeine on reducing gut transit time is consistent with previous observations that bitter compounds activate enteric neurons via serotonin-mediated signaling and promote gut motility.
source: This is consistent with previous observations in adult flies that bitter compounds (including caffeine) activate enteric neurons via serotonin-mediated signaling and promote gut motility (Yao and Scott, 2022).
evidence: This connects the current findings to prior literature through citation.

claim: TaG-EM data recapitulated the results seen in the manual gut transit assay.
source: As with prior behavioral tests, the TaG-EM data recapitulated the results seen in the manual assay (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is directly supported by comparison of data in Figure 4C and 4D.

claim: 19 out of 20 TaG-EM lines showed GFP expression in the expected characteristic central stripe in the wing imaginal disc when crossed to dpp-Gal4.
source: We observed GFP expression in the expected characteristic central stripe (Teleman and Cohen, 2000) in the wing imaginal disc for 19/20 lines at similar expression levels to the base pJFRC12 UAS-myr::GFP construct inserted in the same landing site (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is directly supported by imaging data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: No GFP expression was visible for TaG-EM barcode number 8.
source: No GFP expression was visible for TaG-EM barcode number 8, which upon molecular characterization had an 853 bp deletion within the GFP coding region (data not shown).
evidence: This is an observation from experimental characterization of the lines.

claim: All 156 additional TaG-EM lines had robust GFP expression when crossed to Mhc-Gal4.
source: We generated and tested GFP expression of an additional 156 TaG-EM barcode lines (Alegria et al., 2024), by crossing them to Mhc-Gal4 and observing expression in the adult thorax. All 156 additional TaG-EM lines had robust GFP expression (data not shown).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental observations, though the data is not shown in this manuscript.

claim: Gal4-driven expression levels of TaG-EM barcoded GFP constructs were similar to that of the pJFRC12 base construct for multiple driver lines.
source: Gal4-driven expression levels of TaG-EM barcoded GFP constructs were also similar to that of the pJFRC12 base construct for multiple driver lines (Figure 5—figure supplement 2) indicating that the presence of the barcode does not generally impair expression of GFP.
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Adding an additional hexameric GFP construct could boost expression of weak driver lines to levels sufficient for robust detection.
source: While with some driver lines, expression of the myr::GFP from the TaG-EM construct may be too weak to allow robust enrichment of the tagged cells, adding an additional hexameric GFP construct (Shearin et al., 2014) could boost expression of weak driver lines to levels that are sufficient for robust detection of labeled flies or larvae (Figure 5B) and for labeling of dissociated cells for flow cytometry (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by imaging and flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: TaG-EM barcodes were detected in single-cell sequencing data from intestinal precursor cells driven by PC-Gal4.
source: Expression of all three PC-Gal4-driven TaG-EM barcodes was observed in this cluster (Figure 6—figure supplement 3) indicating that TaG-EM barcodes can be detected in single-cell sequencing data.
evidence: This is directly supported by single-cell sequencing data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: TaG-EM barcode 8, for which no GFP expression was observed, was represented in the single-cell sequencing data.
source: Interestingly, TaG-EM barcode 8, for which no GFP expression was observed, was represented in the single-cell sequencing data indicating that the lesion in the GFP coding region does not prevent mRNA expression for this line.
evidence: This is an observation from single-cell sequencing data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: DoubletFinder identified 2019 multiplet droplets in the single-cell sequencing experiment.
source: DoubletFinder identified 2019 multiplet droplets, while TaG-EM barcodes identified 298 such droplets, 198 of which (66.4%) overlapped with those identified by DoubletFinder (Figure 6—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is directly supported by computational analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 5.

claim: TaG-EM barcodes identified 298 multiplet droplets in the single-cell sequencing experiment.
source: DoubletFinder identified 2019 multiplet droplets, while TaG-EM barcodes identified 298 such droplets, 198 of which (66.4%) overlapped with those identified by DoubletFinder (Figure 6—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is directly supported by computational analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 5.

claim: TaG-EM helped identify an additional 100 doublets that would have been overlooked using computational doublet identification methods alone.
source: Thus, TaG-EM help identify an additional 100 doublets that would have otherwise been overlooked using computational doublet identification methods.
evidence: This is calculated from the data showing 298 TaG-EM-identified doublets minus 198 overlapping with DoubletFinder.

claim: TaG-EM barcodes were observed in approximately one-quarter of the cells in the larval gut single-cell sequencing experiment.
source: TaG-EM barcodes derived from the eight multiplexed genotypes were observed in approximately one-quarter of the cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This is directly supported by single-cell sequencing data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 7.

claim: TaG-EM barcode 6, driven by the EB-Gal4 line, was expressed primarily in cells that were annotated as enteroblasts.
source: For instance, TaG-EM barcode 6, driven by the EB-Gal4 line, was expressed primarily in cells that were annotated as enteroblasts (Figure 6C–D) and that expressed precursor cell markers such as esg (Figure 6E), klu (Figure 6F), and Notch pathway genes such as e(spl)mbeta-HLH and e(spl)m3-HLH (not shown).
evidence: This is directly supported by single-cell sequencing data shown in Figure 6C-F.

claim: TaG-EM barcode 4 expression, driven by the EC-Gal4 line, was seen primarily in a cluster annotated as enterocytes.
source: TaG-EM barcode 4 expression, which was driven by the EC-Gal4 line, was seen primarily in a cluster that was annotated as enterocytes (Figure 6G–H) and that expressed enterocyte markers such as the serine protease Jon99Ciii and other enterocyte marker genes such as the amylase, Amy-d (not shown), but not the beta-Trypsin (betaTry) gene (Figure 6I–J).
evidence: This is directly supported by single-cell sequencing data shown in Figure 6G-J.

claim: The EC-Gal4 line labeled a high percentage of enterocytes, but expression was restricted to the anterior and middle of the midgut, with gaps between these regions and at the posterior.
source: Detailed characterization of the EC-Gal4 line indicated that although this line labeled a high percentage of enterocytes, expression was restricted to an area at the anterior and middle of the midgut, with gaps between these regions and at the posterior (Figure 6—figure supplement 11).
evidence: This is directly supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 11.

claim: TaG-EM barcode 9, expressed using the EE-Gal4 driver line, was observed in clusters annotated as enteroendocrine cells.
source: Finally, expression of TaG-EM barcode 9, which was expressed using the EE-Gal4 driver line, was observed in clusters annotated as enteroendocrine cells (Figure 6K–L) and that also expressed enteroendocrine cell derived neuropeptide genes such as Dh31 (Figure 6M) and other enteroendocrine markers such as IA-2, a tyrosine phosphatase involved in the secretion of insulin-like peptide (Figure 6N).
evidence: This is directly supported by single-cell sequencing data shown in Figure 6K-N.

claim: The EE-Gal4 driver line labeled approximately 80-85% of Prospero-positive enteroendocrine cells in the anterior and middle of the larval midgut.
source: Detailed characterization of the EE-Gal4 driver line indicated that ~80–85% of Prospero-positive enteroendocrine cells are labeled in the anterior and middle of the larval midgut, with a lower percentage (~65%) of Prospero-positive cells labeled in the posterior midgut (Figure 6—figure supplement 11).
evidence: This is directly supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 11.

claim: TaG-EM can be used to label specific cell populations that correlate with Gal4-driven expression patterns in vivo for subsequent identification in single-cell sequencing data.
source: Taken together, these results demonstrate that TaG-EM can be used to label specific cell populations that correlate with Gal4-driven expression patterns in vivo for subsequent identification in single-cell sequencing data.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the multiple experiments showing correlation between Gal4 expression patterns and TaG-EM barcode detection in single-cell data.

claim: Using the enriched TaG-EM barcode library, TaG-EM barcodes were detected in nearly 100% of the cells at high sequencing depths.
source: Using the enriched library, TaG-EM barcodes were detected in nearly 100% of the cells at high sequencing depths (Figure 6—figure supplement 9).
evidence: This is directly supported by data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 9.

claim: For TaG-EM barcode detections where the most abundant barcode was 75-99.99% of the total barcode reads detected, there was a high correlation between the barcode detected in the gene expression library and the enriched TaG-EM barcode library.
source: For TaG-EM barcode detections where the most abundance barcode was a high percentage of the total barcode reads detected (~75%–99.99%), there was a high correlation between the barcode detected in the gene expression library and the enriched TaG-EM barcode library.
evidence: This is directly supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 9.

claim: In the enriched library, 26.8% of cells had a TaG-EM barcode reliably detected.
source: In the enriched library, we identified 26.8% of cells with a TaG-EM barcode reliably detected, a very modest improvement over the gene expression library alone (23.96%), indicating that at least for this experiment, the main constraint is sufficient expression of the TaG-EM barcode and not detection.
evidence: This is directly supported by analysis of the enriched library data.

claim: In the combined data set using both gene expression and enriched libraries, approximately 37% of cells had a barcode identified.
source: This increased the total fraction of cells where a barcode was identified to approximately 37% (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is directly supported by data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: RABID-Seq relies on stochastic viral infection of mammalian cells while TaG-EM allows reproducible targeting of defined cell populations.
source: However, one distinction between the two approaches is that RABID-Seq relies on stochastic viral infection of mammalian cells while TaG-EM allows reproducible targeting of defined cell populations allowing unambiguous cell identification and potentially allowing the same cell populations to be assessed at different timepoints or in the context of different experimental manipulations.
evidence: This is a comparison between TaG-EM and RABID-Seq based on the design principles of each method.

claim: TaG-EM barcodes are not observed in all cells in single-cell gene expression data.
source: One current limitation is that TaG-EM barcodes are not observed in all cells in single-cell gene expression data.
evidence: This is an observation from the single-cell sequencing experiments showing incomplete barcode detection.

claim: The strength of the Gal4 driver likely contributes to TaG-EM barcode labeling density.
source: It is likely that the strength of the Gal4 driver contributes to the labeling density.
evidence: This is an inference based on observations of variable barcode recovery with different drivers.

claim: Variable recovery of TaG-EM barcodes was observed even when all were driven by the same pan-midgut Gal4 driver.
source: However, we also observed variable recovery of TaG-EM barcodes that were all driven by the same pan-midgut Gal4 driver (Figure 6—figure supplement 10).
evidence: This is directly supported by data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 10.

claim: For the specific drivers tested, TaG-EM barcodes are detected in around one quarter of the cells if relying on endogenous expression in the gene expression library.
source: Our experiments indicated that for the specific drivers we tested TaG-EM barcodes are detected in around one quarter of the cells if relying on endogenous expression in the gene expression library, though this fraction was higher (~37%) if sequencing an enriched TaG-EM barcode library in parallel (Figure 6, Figure 6—figure supplement 8 and Figure 6—figure supplement 9).
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data from the single-cell sequencing experiments.
